title: China-to-Portugal EV Charger Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.target_requirement: EU public AC recharging points are subject to AFIR (Regulation (EU) 2023/1804) requirements for connector availability. AFIR Annex II specifies Type 2 for normal-power AC recharging points. IEC/EN 62196-2 describes the Type 2 technical connector design; the legal obligation is AFIR, while the IEC/EN standard is the technical specification route. Portugal, as an EU member state, is subject to AFIR directly without need for national transposition.
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB/T 20234.2 for AC charging, which defines a physically distinct 7-pin connector incompatible with IEC Type 2. GB/T plugs cannot mate with EU Type 2 sockets.
rows.gap: Hardware connector is physically incompatible. A Chinese EV or EVSE designed only around a GB/T AC interface cannot interoperate with EU/Portugal public Type 2 AC infrastructure without a physical inlet/socket and control-interface redesign. The connector body, pin count, and locking mechanism all differ. Any adapter strategy for public infrastructure must be checked against AFIR and local Portuguese/EU safety rules rather than treated as a substitute for compliant connector design.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: AFIR requirements for publicly accessible AC recharging points, including Type 2 availability as specified in Annex II, apply directly in Portugal from 13 April 2024. IEC/EN 62196-2 is the voluntary technical connector standard/specification used to implement that legal requirement; it is not the legal obligation by itself.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory in China for domestic market — GB/T 20234.2 required for EV sold in China

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Non-compliant for EU/Portugal public charging interoperability as-is if the product only supports GB/T AC. EU/Portugal public AC infrastructure must meet AFIR connector requirements, and IEC/EN 62196-2 Type 2 is the technical specification used for that route. GB/T AC interfaces are not a substitute for AFIR-compliant Type 2 compatibility.

rows.target_requirement: EU public DC recharging points are subject to AFIR (Regulation (EU) 2023/1804) requirements for connector availability. AFIR Annex II specifies Combo 2 for high-power DC recharging points. IEC/EN 62196-3 describes the CCS Combo 2 technical connector design; the legal obligation is AFIR, while the IEC/EN standard is the technical specification route. Portugal is subject to AFIR directly as an EU member state.
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB/T 20234.3 for DC fast charging, defining a physically distinct 9-pin connector (CHAdeMO-influenced design) incompatible with CCS Combo 2. The pin layout, communication protocol (CAN vs. PLC), and inlet shape all differ.
rows.gap: Hardware connector is physically incompatible. Chinese EVs or EVSE with only a GB/T DC interface cannot fast-charge at EU/Portugal CCS2 public stations without hardware and communication-stack redesign. The vehicle/charger communication stack (GB/T 27930 CAN vs. ISO 15118 / DIN 70121 PLC pathways in common EU CCS practice) also differs, compounding the incompatibility beyond the physical plug. Any adapter strategy for public infrastructure must be checked against AFIR and local Portuguese/EU safety rules.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: AFIR requirements for publicly accessible high-power DC recharging points, including Combo 2 availability as specified in Annex II, apply directly in Portugal from 13 April 2024. IEC/EN 62196-3 is the voluntary technical connector standard/specification used to implement that legal requirement; it is not the legal obligation by itself.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory in China for domestic market — GB/T 20234.3 required for DC fast-charge EV sold in China

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Non-compliant for EU/Portugal public DC charging interoperability as-is if the product only supports GB/T DC. EU/Portugal public DC infrastructure must meet AFIR connector requirements, and IEC/EN 62196-3 CCS Combo 2 is the technical specification used for that route. GB/T DC interfaces are not a substitute for AFIR-compliant Combo 2 compatibility.

rows.requirement: Legal Mandate: AFIR vs. AFID and Transition Timeline
rows.target_requirement: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 (AFIR) replaced Directive 2014/94/EU (AFID) with binding targets. AFIR entered into force 13 April 2024. New public charging pools must comply from that date; all existing pools must be upgraded to Type 2 / CCS2 by 2025–2026 depending on power level. AFIR is directly applicable in all EU member states without transposition, including Portugal.
rows.china_equivalent: China's equivalent policy mandate is GB/T 20234 series (enforced via MIIT type-approval). No bilateral connector recognition or mutual acceptance agreement exists between China GB/T and EU IEC 62196 standards. (Confirmed: no bilateral connector or certification mutual recognition treaty between CN GB/T 20234 and EU IEC 62196 has been concluded as of June 2026.)
rows.gap: No harmonisation or mutual recognition between GB/T and IEC 62196 series. AFIR is a binding EU Regulation (not a Directive), meaning no member-state flexibility to accept GB/T connectors, including in Portugal. Any EV destined for the Portugal/EU market must carry Type 2 (AC) and CCS Combo 2 (DC) inlets as a hard market-entry requirement.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: AFIR is directly applicable across EU member states, including Portugal, from 13 April 2024 for in-scope publicly accessible recharging infrastructure. IEC/EN 62196 connector standards are technical specifications referenced/used to implement AFIR connector requirements, not standalone legal obligations.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory domestically; no reciprocal obligation on EU/Portugal side to accept GB/T

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Non-compliant as-is for EU/Portugal public charging infrastructure where a product relies on Chinese GB/T connectors only. AFIR creates the binding EU obligation for in-scope public infrastructure; Type 2 / Combo 2 technical compatibility is the practical redesign item. This is a product and infrastructure interoperability gap, not merely a documentation gap.

source.publisher: ERSE — Entidade Reguladora dos Serviços Energéticos (Portugal energy regulator)

rows.requirement: E-Redes Grid Connection — 230/400 V 50 Hz Portuguese Network
rows.target_requirement: Portugal's electricity distribution network is operated by E-Redes (formerly EDP Distribuição), with sector oversight by ERSE (Entidade Reguladora dos Serviços Energéticos) and transmission by REN (Redes Energéticas Nacionais). The low-voltage context is 230 V single-phase / 400 V three-phase at 50 Hz. That is the same frequency as China but a different nominal voltage from China's 220/380 V baseline. Grid-connected charger projects should be treated as site-specific electrical installations requiring E-Redes supply-capacity review, protection coordination, metering, earthing, harmonic and power-quality review, commissioning, and written project acceptance (Protocolo de Ligação) before energisation. For publicly accessible chargers, ERSE oversees AFIR compliance and DGEG (Direção-Geral de Energia e Geologia) provides energy-sector oversight for larger installations.
target_standards: E-Redes — Manual de Ligações (electricity network connection and project acceptance)
ERSE — Entidade Reguladora dos Serviços Energéticos (energy sector oversight)
IEC 61000 series — electromagnetic compatibility and power quality
IEC 61851-1 — EV conductive charging system general requirements
DGEG — Direção-Geral de Energia e Geologia (energy and geology directorate-general)
rows.china_equivalent: China domestic charger installations are commonly documented under GB/T 18487.1-2023, GB/T 20234 connector standards, GB/T 27930-2023 for DC communication, and local grid-operator acceptance. China domestic supply is 220 V single-phase / 380 V three-phase at 50 Hz. The shared 50 Hz frequency does not mean voltage equivalence: Portugal 230/400 V requires input-voltage, protection-threshold, thermal, and metering validation beyond the China baseline.
china_standards: China local grid operator project-acceptance requirements
rows.gap: Exporters must confirm that the charger covers 230 V single-phase / 400 V three-phase at 50 Hz, not only China's 220/380 V settings. Protection thresholds, leakage-current devices, metering accuracy, harmonic emissions, supply-capacity calculations, earthing, surge protection, and commissioning documents should be prepared for E-Redes review. The E-Redes Protocolo de Ligação process requires site-specific documentation including ITED (Infraestruturas de Telecomunicações em Edifícios) and ITUR (Infraestruturas de Telecomunicações em Loteamentos, Urbanizações e Conjuntos de Edifícios) compliance where applicable. Portuguese-language technical documentation is required for E-Redes review.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — grid-connected installations require E-Redes project review and Protocolo de Ligação acceptance; voltage is 230/400 V at 50 Hz, which differs from China 220/380 V despite the same frequency
mandatory_status.cn: China grid-operator acceptance applies domestically and is not an E-Redes / Portugal approval substitute; China 220/380 V evidence must be revalidated for Portugal 230/400 V

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Portugal-ready EVSE needs E-Redes project acceptance and explicit 230/400 V 50 Hz validation. Do not describe the voltage as matching China: only the 50 Hz frequency matches, while nominal voltage differs from China's 220/380 V baseline. Portuguese-language technical documentation is required for E-Redes review.

source.publisher: ERSE — Entidade Reguladora dos Serviços Energéticos (Portugal energy regulator)

rows.requirement: CE Conformity Assessment — LVD, EMC, RED (if wireless)
rows.target_requirement: EV chargers sold in Portugal / EU must bear the CE marking, demonstrating conformity with all applicable EU legislation. Wired AC/DC chargers typically fall under LVD (2014/35/EU) and EMC Directive (2014/30/EU); chargers with wireless communication (e.g., Wi-Fi, Bluetooth for smart charging) additionally require conformity with RED (2014/53/EU). Conformity is generally established by manufacturer self-declaration supported by a technical file. Harmonised EN standards are voluntary routes to presumption of conformity, not mandatory legal requirements in themselves. In Portugal, ASAE and DGConsumidor are the market surveillance authorities for product safety.
target_standards: EN IEC 61851-21-2 (EMC for off-board EV chargers)
rows.china_equivalent: In China, EV chargers require China Compulsory Certification (CCC) under the GB/T and GB standards regime. Key standards include GB/T 18487.1 (AC charging system) and GB/T 20234 series (connectors). CCC is a mandatory third-party certification through designated bodies (CABs); it does not involve self-declaration and is structurally different from CE's conformity-based model.
rows.gap: Chinese manufacturers must obtain CE marking via EU-recognised conformity assessment routes (self-declaration under harmonised EN standards or notified-body involvement for certain RED equipment). CCC certification is not recognised in Portugal/EU and does not substitute for CE. Manufacturers must generate EU-specific technical documentation, test reports referencing EN standards, and an EU Declaration of Conformity — none of which are produced as part of the CCC process. Portuguese-language product instructions are commonly expected for the Portugal market.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: CE marking and conformity with all applicable EU directives/regulations before EU/Portugal market access. Harmonised EN standards are voluntary presumption-of-conformity tools; alternatives are allowed if compliance is demonstrated.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] CE marking is mandatory before placing EV chargers on the Portugal/EU market. CCC does not substitute for CE. Manufacturers must independently build EU technical files and, for wireless-enabled chargers, ensure RED compliance where applicable. Harmonised EN standards may support presumption of conformity but are not the mandatory legal obligation themselves. Portuguese-language product documentation is expected for the Portugal market.

source.publisher: ERSE — Entidade Reguladora dos Serviços Energéticos (Portugal energy regulator)

rows.requirement: EU Declaration of Conformity (DoC) and Technical File
rows.target_requirement: Before placing a product on the Portugal/EU market, the manufacturer (or its EU authorised representative) must draw up an EU Declaration of Conformity (DoC) listing all applicable directives and the harmonised standards applied, and must compile and retain a technical file for at least 10 years. The DoC must be made available to market surveillance authorities (in Portugal: ASAE / DGConsumidor) on request. Requirements are set out in each applicable directive (LVD Art. 15, EMCD Art. 14, RED Art. 19) and in Decision 768/2008/EC (modular conformity assessment).
rows.china_equivalent: Under the Chinese CCC regime, the equivalent documentary output is the CCC certificate issued by the designated certification body, accompanied by type-test reports. There is no manufacturer self-declaration equivalent to the EU DoC; the certificate is issued by a third party. Post-certificate, manufacturers must maintain a production consistency system audited periodically by the CAB.
china_standards: CNCA-C25-01:2024 (CCC implementation rules for EV charging equipment — effective 1 March 2025, supersedes any prior voluntary-only scheme; issued CNCA Announcement No. 25/2024)
Measures for the Administration of Compulsory Product Certification (SAMR 2020)
rows.gap: Chinese manufacturers exporting to Portugal/EU must create an EU-format DoC from scratch — listing each applicable EU directive, the specific harmonised standards applied, the manufacturer's name and address (or EU authorised representative's), and a traceable signatory. The CCC certificate neither replaces nor simplifies this; test data generated for CCC may be re-used only if it was produced against equivalent EN test methods, which requires engineering review. The DoC must be available in Portuguese and/or another EU language accepted by ASAE upon request.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — must accompany product or be available on request from ASAE / DGConsumidor (Portugal market surveillance authorities)
mandatory_status.cn: N/A — replaced by third-party CCC certificate regime

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] An EU DoC is a legal document that manufacturers or their EU representatives must sign and retain. It cannot be delegated to a test lab or certification body. Chinese exporters with only CCC documentation must draft the DoC in-house or engage an EU-based compliance consultant. The DoC and product technical documentation should be available in Portuguese for the Portugal market.

source.publisher: ERSE — Entidade Reguladora dos Serviços Energéticos (Portugal energy regulator)

rows.requirement: EU Economic Operator / Authorised Representative — Regulation (EU) 2019/1020
rows.target_requirement: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 on market surveillance and product compliance requires that products placed on the EU market have an identifiable 'responsible economic operator' established in the EU. For products manufactured outside the EU, this means the importer or, if no EU importer, a mandated EU authorised representative (Art. 4). The responsible operator must: hold the DoC and technical file or ensure they are accessible; register in RAPEX/ICSMS where required; cooperate with market surveillance authorities (in Portugal: ASAE / DGConsumidor); and take corrective action if a product is non-compliant. This obligation applies to EV chargers as CE-marked electrical equipment.
rows.china_equivalent: China has no direct regulatory equivalent requiring a domestic responsible operator for export-bound products. Chinese manufacturers exporting abroad appoint foreign distributors or agents commercially, but there is no statutory requirement to designate an EU-resident legal representative responsible for CE compliance and market surveillance cooperation.
rows.gap: This is a structural gap with no Chinese regulatory analogue. A Chinese EV charger manufacturer shipping directly to Portuguese customers (e.g., via e-commerce) must appoint an EU-established authorised representative before the first unit enters the Portugal/EU market. Without one, the product cannot legally be placed on the Portugal/EU market under Regulation 2019/1020. The AR must be named on the product label or documentation.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for non-EU manufacturers without an EU importer — applies equally to the Portugal market

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Chinese manufacturers without an EU importer must appoint an EU-established authorised representative. This is a hard legal gate under Regulation 2019/1020 — no EU AR means the product cannot lawfully enter the Portugal/EU market, regardless of CE marking status.

source.publisher: ERSE — Entidade Reguladora dos Serviços Energéticos (Portugal energy regulator)

rows.requirement: AFIR — Public EV Charging: Ad-hoc Payment, Interoperability and Technical Specifications
rows.target_requirement: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 (AFIR) mandates functional requirements for publicly accessible EV recharging points. AFIR-confirmed requirements include: (1) ad-hoc charging without a subscription or contract, with the payment instruments required by AFIR for relevant publicly accessible recharging points; (2) transparent price information before a charging session starts; (3) digital connectivity, smart recharging capability, static data and dynamic data obligations for publicly accessible infrastructure; (4) AFIR Annex II technical specifications for publicly accessible recharging points, including Type 2 for normal-power AC recharging points and Combo 2 for high-power DC recharging points; and (5) TEN-T deployment targets for recharging pools. AFIR replaces Directive 2014/94/EU (AFID) and applies directly in Portugal.
target_standards: AFIR Annex II (technical specifications for publicly accessible recharging points)
rows.china_equivalent: China has no direct regulatory equivalent to AFIR's functional public-charging requirements. The closest standards are GB/T 34658 (interoperability requirements) and NB/T 33025 (communication protocols for EV charging), plus GB/T 27930 (DC charging communication). Chinese public chargers are increasingly connected via operator platforms (e.g., State Grid, Southern Grid, TELD), but AFIR-equivalent ad-hoc payment, data-access, smart recharging and EU connector requirements are not mandated by Chinese regulation.
china_standards: NB/T 33025-2016 (EV DC charging communication protocol — EVSE side)
GB/T 27930-2015 (communication protocol between off-board charger and BMS)
rows.gap: Significant functional gap for public charging deployments in Portugal: (1) ad-hoc payment functionality may need to be added for EU/Portuguese public deployments, with Multibanco / MB Way payment acceptance expected in some Portuguese tenders; (2) digital connectivity, smart recharging, data-access and roaming/data exchange obligations may differ from proprietary Chinese operator platforms; (3) AFIR Annex II connector specifications differ from Chinese GB/T connector practice. These AFIR requirements apply primarily to charge point operators (CPOs), but hardware and software capability must be available at installation. ERSE supervises AFIR compliance in Portugal.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for publicly accessible recharging points in Portugal/EU under Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 (AFIR), directly applicable from 13 April 2024.
mandatory_status.cn: Not mandated — AFIR-equivalent ad-hoc payment, data-access, smart recharging and EU connector requirements are absent from Chinese public charging regulations.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] AFIR introduces functional requirements for publicly accessible charging points in Portugal/EU, including ad-hoc payment, price transparency, digital connectivity, smart recharging, data obligations and Annex II connector specifications. Chinese charger hardware intended for Portuguese public deployment must be verified for AFIR compliance before installation. ERSE is the Portuguese supervisory authority for AFIR compliance.

source.publisher: ERSE — Entidade Reguladora dos Serviços Energéticos (Portugal energy regulator)

rows.requirement: OCPP, EMC, Radio Modules, and Power Quality
rows.target_requirement: Networked EV chargers in Portugal should be specified for OCPP back-office interoperability where a charge-point operator, municipal authority, public-sector project, ERSE-regulated operator, or E-Redes-linked programme requires remote monitoring, billing, diagnostics, or load management. Electrical and electronic emissions and immunity evidence should align with IEC 61000 EMC and power-quality standards. Cellular, Wi-Fi, RFID, payment (including Multibanco / MB Way for publicly accessible Portuguese charging infrastructure), or smart-metering modules may trigger additional communications, spectrum, cybersecurity, and data-interface checks under AFIR and Portuguese national requirements. The Portuguese communications regulator ANACOM oversees radio spectrum and device type approvals for wireless modules.
target_standards: OCPP — Open Charge Point Protocol for networked EV chargers
IEC 61000 series — electromagnetic compatibility and power quality
IEC 61851-24 — digital communication between DC EV charging station and EV
ANACOM — Autoridade Nacional de Comunicações (Portugal communications regulator) for radio module spectrum approvals
AFIR — Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 for data, connectivity, and smart recharging obligations at publicly accessible recharging points in Portugal
rows.china_equivalent: China DC fast chargers commonly use GB/T 27930-2023 CAN communication between the off-board charger and vehicle BMS. This is not OCPP back-office communication and is not the CCS2 communication direction. China-market chargers may also include China-specific payment (WeChat Pay, Alipay), SIM, cloud, and operator integrations that need reconfiguration for Portuguese/EU operators, roaming, language (Portuguese), currency (EUR), and data interfaces.
china_standards: China radio module approvals where applicable
rows.gap: Exporters must confirm the OCPP version, charge-point-management-system integration, remote diagnostics, load management, payment or RFID flow (including Multibanco/MB Way for publicly accessible Portuguese infrastructure), SIM or communications module ANACOM approval path, and IEC 61000 EMC reports for the final Portugal configuration. For DC CCS2 products, GB/T 27930 must not be presented as the relevant communication evidence. Harmonic current and immunity data should be reviewed against the specific E-Redes supply point constraints. AFIR data and connectivity requirements for publicly accessible infrastructure are mandatory in Portugal from April 2024.

mandatory_status.target: Project-specific but commonly mandatory for networked public, fleet, or utility-linked chargers in Portugal; EMC and power-quality evidence is expected where required by ERSE, E-Redes, ANACOM, AFIR, tender, or site-owner specifications; AFIR data and smart recharging obligations apply to publicly accessible recharging points
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 27930 is China domestic DC vehicle-charger communication and is not OCPP or CCS2 back-office evidence

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Portugal networked chargers should be validated for OCPP integration, IEC 61000 EMC and power quality, AFIR data and smart-recharging compliance, and local communications-module ANACOM requirements. GB/T 27930 alone does not satisfy OCPP, CCS2 communication, or back-office interoperability needs. Multibanco/MB Way payment integration may be required for publicly accessible Portuguese charging infrastructure.

source.publisher: ERSE — Entidade Reguladora dos Serviços Energéticos (Portugal energy regulator)

rows.requirement: Low Voltage Safety — EV Charging Equipment (General)
rows.target_requirement: EV charging equipment placed on the Portugal/EU market must comply with the Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU, ensuring it is designed and manufactured to be safe when correctly installed and maintained. Equipment must meet the Essential Safety Requirements (Annex I) covering protection against electric shock, insulation, overcurrent/overtemperature protection, and clearances. Harmonised standard EN IEC 61851-1:2019 (Mode 1–4 conductive charging, AC and DC, general requirements) provides a presumption of conformity. In Portugal, ASAE and DGConsumidor are the market surveillance authorities for product safety compliance with LVD.
target_standards: EN IEC 61851-1:2019 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — Part 1: General requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly references GB/T 18487.1-2015 (Electric vehicle conductive charging system — General requirements), which is technically aligned with IEC 61851-1 but incorporates national deviations. It is enforced under the GB framework administered by SAMR/SAC. GB/T 18487.1 testing and certification by a Chinese CNAS-accredited lab is NOT recognised as equivalent to EN IEC 61851-1 testing under the EU LVD conformity assessment pathway.
china_standards: GB/T 18487.1-2015 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — General requirements (SAMR/SAC)
rows.gap: Exporters should build an EU conformity file against the LVD essential safety requirements and may use EN IEC 61851-1:2019 testing as evidence for presumption of conformity. Existing Chinese GB/T 18487.1 test reports do not automatically substitute because scope, deviations, connector assumptions and documentation differ. A Notified Body is not mandatory for LVD; manufacturer self-declaration with a Technical File is the normal route. Documentation gap: EU Declaration of Conformity, CE marking, and EU/Portuguese-language technical instructions are all required. The charger configuration must be validated for Portugal's 230/400 V 50 Hz supply, not China's 220/380 V.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: Directive 2014/35/EU and CE marking before Portugal/EU market placement. EN IEC 61851-1:2019 is voluntary harmonised-standard evidence for presumption of conformity; alternative technical solutions are allowed if the manufacturer demonstrates compliance with the LVD essential safety requirements.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for domestic market — GB/T 18487.1 compliance required under SAMR framework

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] CE marking under LVD 2014/35/EU is mandatory before placing EV chargers on the Portugal/EU market. EN IEC 61851-1:2019 is a voluntary harmonised standard that can grant presumption of conformity for general EV conductive charging; it is not the legal obligation itself. Chinese GB/T 18487.1 certification does not by itself satisfy the EU conformity assessment pathway; EU evidence against the LVD requirements is needed. Product configuration and labelling must reflect Portugal's 230/400 V 50 Hz supply.

rows.requirement: DC Charging Station Safety — EV Conductive Charging
rows.target_requirement: DC charging stations (Mode 4, off-board chargers) placed on the Portugal/EU market must comply with the Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU where within scope. EN IEC 61851-23:2023 (Electric vehicle conductive charging system — Part 23: DC EV charging station) is a current product standard that may be used as technical evidence and, where cited as harmonised, gives presumption of conformity; it is not itself the mandatory legal obligation. Key technical topics include isolation monitoring, interlock systems, control pilot functions, maximum voltage/current ratings, and communication protocols for DC supply. For Portugal, the CCS2 (IEC 62196-3) connector is the required public DC charging interface under AFIR.
target_standards: EN IEC 61851-23:2023 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — Part 23: DC EV charging station (current edition, supersedes 2014)
IEC 62196-3 / EN 62196-3 — CCS Combo 2 DC connector (required by AFIR for Portugal/EU public DC charging)
rows.china_equivalent: China's DC charging station domestic equivalent is GB/T 18487.3-2001 (AC/DC electric vehicle charging station — the only published Part 3 of the 18487 series; note: a GB/T 18487.3-2015 does not exist). The current DC system standard is GB/T 18487.5-2024 (DC charging system for GB/T 20234.3 connector). The DC coupler standard is GB/T 20234.3-2023. CQC or CNAS certification to these Chinese standards is not accepted under the EU LVD CE marking pathway.
china_standards: GB/T 18487.3-2001 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — AC/DC electric vehicle charging station (only published edition; no 2015 revision exists)
GB/T 18487.5-2024 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — Part 5: DC charging system for GB/T 20234.3 (current DC system standard)
GB/T 20234.3-2023 — Connection set for conductive charging of electric vehicles — Part 3: DC charging coupler (supersedes 2015 edition)
rows.gap: DC charging stations exported to Portugal/EU should be assessed against the LVD essential safety requirements and may use EN IEC 61851-23:2023 testing as presumption-of-conformity evidence where applicable. Particular attention is needed for: (1) CCS2 (Combined Charging System Type 2) connector compliance required under AFIR for Portuguese public DC charging vs. Chinese GB/T connector; (2) isolation monitoring requirements per European grid topology; and (3) ISO 15118 / DIN 70121 PLC communication compatibility for CCS2 vs. Chinese GB/T 27930 CAN protocol. The connector type itself is a hardware gap — Chinese DC stations typically use GB/T 20234.3 plugs, which are not CCS2 compatible without hardware redesign. Portuguese-language installation and safety documentation is required for E-Redes review.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: CE marking under Directive 2014/35/EU where the charger is within LVD scope; CCS2 connector mandatory under AFIR for Portugal/EU public DC charging infrastructure from 13 April 2024. EN IEC 61851-23:2023 is a voluntary technical standard that may support presumption of conformity where harmonised/cited.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory — GB/T 18487.5-2024 is the current DC charging system standard; CCC mandatory from 1 March 2025 under CNCA-C25-01:2024

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] DC charging stations require CE marking under the applicable EU legislation, including LVD where in scope. For Portugal/EU public DC charging, CCS2 (IEC 62196-3) connector is mandated by AFIR. EN IEC 61851-23:2023 is a voluntary product standard used as technical evidence or presumption-of-conformity support where harmonised; it is not mandatory in itself. Chinese GB/T 18487.3 certification is not accepted as an EU conformity assessment substitute. A significant hardware gap exists where Chinese DC stations use GB/T connectors incompatible with EU CCS2 practice.

rows.requirement: Electrical Installation Safety — EV Charging in Buildings (IEC 60364-7-722)
rows.target_requirement: EU member-state electrical installation law and grid/installer rules govern the building-side circuits supplying EV charging points. IEC 60364-7-722 / HD 60364-7-722 provide the commonly adopted technical installation route covering protective measures (RCD type B or A+DC detection), wiring, earthing, and load management. In Portugal, electrical installation regulations are set by the RTIEBT (Regras Técnicas das Instalações Elétricas de Baixa Tensão), which is the Portuguese low-voltage electrical installation code adopted under DL 226/2005 and updated by subsequent legislation. E-Redes connection approval (Protocolo de Ligação) requires RTIEBT-compliant installation documentation. These standards apply to the building-side installation infrastructure, not the charger product itself, but exported EV chargers should be compatible with these installation requirements.
target_standards: IEC 60364-7-722:2018 — Low-voltage electrical installations — Part 7-722: Requirements for special installations or locations — Supply of electric vehicles
HD 60364-7-722 (CENELEC harmonised document, adopted by EU member states)
RTIEBT — Regras Técnicas das Instalações Elétricas de Baixa Tensão (Portugal low-voltage electrical installation technical rules, DL 226/2005 and subsequent amendments)
rows.china_equivalent: China addresses EV charging installation primarily through GB 50966-2014 (Code for design of electric vehicle charging station) and GB/T 51313-2018 (Technical standard for electric vehicle charging infrastructure), administered by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (MOHURD). These cover site design and installation but differ from IEC 60364-7-722 and Portuguese RTIEBT in RCD type requirements, earthing system assumptions, and load management protocols. Chinese installation documentation is not accepted as evidence of compliance with Portuguese RTIEBT or EU member-state installation standards.
china_standards: GB 50966-2014 — Code for design of electric vehicle charging station (MOHURD) (confirmed to exist; enforced by MOHURD/MIIT)
GB/T 51313-2018 — Technical standard for electric vehicle charging infrastructure (confirmed to exist; enforced by MOHURD/MIIT)
rows.gap: IEC 60364-7-722 / HD 60364-7-722 and the Portuguese RTIEBT are installation standards — they govern fixed wiring and protection devices at the building side, not the charger product itself. However, exported EV chargers should declare compatibility with Type B RCDs or incorporate internal DC fault protection to allow Type A RCDs under EU/Portuguese installation practice. A charger that requires installation conditions not achievable under RTIEBT will fail field acceptance by E-Redes. Chinese charger datasheets often omit RCD compatibility statements expected by Portuguese installers, E-Redes, and DGEG. Portuguese-language installation manuals compatible with RTIEBT terminology are required.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation sits in Portuguese electrical installation law (RTIEBT, DL 226/2005) and E-Redes / DGEG grid codes and permitting rules. rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] IEC 60364-7-722 / HD 60364-7-722 and Portuguese RTIEBT govern building-side installation practice. EV chargers exported to Portugal/EU should be compatible with the RCD and earthing requirements expected by Portuguese installers, E-Redes, and DGEG. This is distinct from product-level CE marking under LVD, but non-compatibility can block field installation and E-Redes Protocolo de Ligação approval. Chinese installation standards (GB 50966 / GB/T 51313) are not substitutes. Portuguese-language installation manuals compatible with RTIEBT are required.
